🇲🇽🌼 <u>Mexico City Grows 9.9 Million Cempasúchil Plants, Up 55%</u>

CDMX produced 9,924,300 cempasúchil plants this year, up from almost 6.5 million in 2025, Clara Brugada said as sales opened in Xochimilco. The number of growers went from 460 to 596, and 87.6% of them get support from the Altépetl Bienestar program, which put more than 8 million pesos into seeds, compost, pots and roads. Pots sell for 15 to 30 pesos. Sedema rejected claims that the flowers are Chinese imports. The ones with the Sello Verde are 100% agroecological.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court Upholds Direct Funding for Indigenous Communities, Rejecting 12 Municipalities</u>

The SCJN ruled unanimously that municipalities must hand at least 10% of the FAIS infrastructure fund directly to Indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities. It threw out 12 constitutional challenges from places like San Nicolás de los Garza, Huixquilucan, Metepec, San Andrés Cholula and CDMX's Cuauhtémoc borough. The Court cited the 2024 reform of Article 2, which recognizes the communities as subjects of public law that can manage their own budgets. In 2026 that share, FAISPIAM, is worth 13.506 billion pesos.

🇲🇽🏺 <u>Six Veracruz Artifacts Stopped at Mexico City Airport Before Shipping to Britain</u>

Customs agents, working with the Navy and the Security Ministry, caught six archaeological pieces from Veracruz in Correos de México's export area at AICM. They were addressed to Great Britain. INAH confirmed they belong to the nation's cultural heritage. Under Mexican law those pieces are inalienable and can't be sold or exported. The FGR now has the seizure. Mexico spends years getting its history back from foreign auction houses, and this time it never left the country.
banner: AICM: 6 ARTIFACTS STOPPED EN ROUTE TO UK

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Pentagon Clears a "Heat Ray" for the Border With Mexico</u>

Hegseth signed off on lending DHS the Active Denial System, a vehicle-mounted microwave weapon, to test and develop tactics for operations on the border with Mexico. The beam reaches almost a kilometer and makes skin feel like it's burning, "like opening the door of a hot oven," according to military officials. The loan runs seven months and DHS can ask for more. The target is migrants and crowds. CBP's answer: it "always evaluates new technologies."

🇲🇽🌎 "What do we want? The best relationship with the United States. Always with respect for our sovereignty." "And that there be no political use of Mexico in the middle of the United States' electoral process." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 21, 2026 A reporter asked why, days after telling Ambassador Ronald Johnson to respect Mexican law over a training-academy deal with Querétaro's government, she called him an ally. Sheinbaum said both are true. He helped lift US sanctions that had blocked new international flights from the US to AIFA and Mexico City's airport. When Mexico disagrees, as when he went to Sinaloa to talk about corruption, it tells him directly. She also asked that the human rights of Mexicans in the US be respected and their work recognized. "That is the truth."
